All corrected and verified:
- `https://SITE.com/Article?ref=A/` is now treated as a **different** page from `…?ref=A` (the slash lives inside the query), so it's saved separately.
- `https://SITE.com/Article/?ref=A` (harmless trailing slash on the path + host capitalisation) **is** caught as the same link.
- In the editor, plain text and non-web addresses (like `ftp://…`) are **rejected** with a clear message; only a real `http`/`https` link saves.

Ready at **http://maker:4001** — please confirm with your own corrected cases:

1. Save `https://site.com/Article?ref=A`. Then save `https://SITE.com/Article?ref=A/` — should be accepted as a **different** page. Then save `https://SITE.com/Article/?ref=A` — should be caught as **already saved** and open it for editing.
2. Open **Edit** on a bookmark, type something that isn't a link (e.g. `hello`) into the **Address** field, and try to save — it should refuse. Then put in a valid link and confirm it saves.

I've also noted your **"refresh page details"** idea (an explicit action to re-fetch details when you deliberately point a bookmark at a different page) for a later refinement — the default stays: correcting an address never overwrites your own title/description.

If this all behaves as you expect, the **saving** step is fully settled and I'll move us on to the next flow — **finding a saved link again**, which was your main goal.
